ai.headline: Hybrid RAG: dense vectors and BM25 keywords are searched together, then fused; keyword hits are expanded through an entity graph; an evidence check sends the question back for more retrieval when the passages are not enough

stages.name: pytesseract
stages.explain: Loads raw documents (PDF, web pages, files) and turns them into text plus metadata.

stages.name: chunk_pages
stages.explain: Chunking. Cuts long text into overlapping pieces small enough to embed and to fit in the prompt. chunk_size is the piece length, chunk_overlap repeats the end of one chunk at the start of the next so a sentence is not lost at the cut.

stages.name: bge-m3-Q8
stages.explain: BGE-M3 embedding model. The model can produce dense, sparse and multi-vector outputs; which of them this app uses depends on what its code stores and searches.

stages.name: pgvector
stages.explain: Vector store. Keeps every chunk's vector with its text and metadata, indexed (often HNSW) for fast nearest-neighbour search.

stages.name: lexical_search
stages.explain: BM25 is keyword search. It scores chunks by how often the query words appear in them, discounted by how common those words are everywhere. It finds exact names and codes that embeddings miss.

stages.name: expand_entities
stages.explain: Graph-assisted retrieval. Starts from the keyword hits, follows linked entities and relations in the graph, and adds the passages they point to.

stages.name: rrf_fuse
stages.explain: Fusion. Merges the dense and keyword result lists into one ranking (often Reciprocal Rank Fusion).

stages.name: CrossEncoder
stages.explain: Reranker (cross-encoder). Reads the question and each candidate chunk together and scores how well they match. Slower than vector search but much more precise, so it re-orders the top-k candidates and keeps the best top-n.

stages.name: evidence_is_sufficient
stages.explain: Evidence check. Decides whether the retrieved passages are enough to answer. If not, retrieval runs again with a wider search; if yes, the passages go on to the answer.

stages.name: Qwen3-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf
stages.explain: Language model call. Reads the prompt and generates the answer token by token; with tools enabled it can answer with a tool call instead.

libraries.name: FastAPI
libraries.explain: Python web API framework; routes are typed functions validated with Pydantic.

libraries.name: React
libraries.explain: Builds UIs from components; re-renders when state changes.

services.name: web
services.explain: Frontend built from this repository (2 source files): the screens the user sees in the browser.

services.name: api
services.explain: Backend API built from this repository (9 source files): receives HTTP requests and runs the app logic.

services.name: embed
services.explain: llama.cpp server: runs quantized GGUF models on CPU or GPU with a small footprint.

services.name: llm
services.explain: llama.cpp server: runs quantized GGUF models on CPU or GPU with a small footprint.

services.name: db
services.explain: Postgres + pgvector: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension: embeddings live in a normal table column and nearest-neighbour search is SQL. Full-text search (tsvector) in the same database gives the keyword half of hybrid search.

hops.label: type “Ask the books”
hops.explain: The user types a question into the input on this screen.

hops.label: onAsk()
hops.explain: Its onClick handler runs in the browser.

hops.label: ask()
hops.explain: A resolved call on the way to the network request.

hops.label: POST /api/ask
hops.explain: The browser sends POST /api/ask; the backend route POST /api/ask receives it and runs ask().

hops.label: hand off to app/src/retrieval.py
hops.explain: ask() uses the pipeline defined in app/src/retrieval.py (matched by import; the call itself is dynamic).

hops.label: lexical_search
hops.explain: seed hits: BM25 is keyword search. It scores chunks by how often the query words appear in them, discounted by how common those words are everywhere. It finds exact names and codes that embeddings miss.

hops.label: db container
hops.explain: The work behind lexical_search happens in its own container. The db container is reached over the network (DATABASE_URL -> db:5432).

hops.label: expand_entities
hops.explain: Graph-assisted retrieval. Starts from the keyword hits, follows linked entities and relations in the graph, and adds the passages they point to. Settings in the code: lane=lexical.

hops.label: bge-m3-Q8
hops.explain: vectors: BGE-M3 embedding model. The model can produce dense, sparse and multi-vector outputs; which of them this app uses depends on what its code stores and searches. Settings in the code: model=bge-m3-Q8.

hops.label: pgvector
hops.explain: nearest-neighbour search: Vector store. Keeps every chunk's vector with its text and metadata, indexed (often HNSW) for fast nearest-neighbour search.

hops.label: rrf_fuse
hops.explain: expanded hits: Fusion. Merges the dense and keyword result lists into one ranking (often Reciprocal Rank Fusion).

hops.label: CrossEncoder
hops.explain: fused candidates: Reranker (cross-encoder). Reads the question and each candidate chunk together and scores how well they match. Slower than vector search but much more precise, so it re-orders the top-k candidates and keeps the best top-n. Settings in the code: model=Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B.

hops.label: evidence_is_sufficient
hops.explain: top-n chunks: Evidence check. Decides whether the retrieved passages are enough to answer. If not, retrieval runs again with a wider search; if yes, the passages go on to the answer. Settings in the code: check=evidence.

hops.label: Qwen3-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf
hops.explain: enough evidence: Language model call. Reads the prompt and generates the answer token by token; with tools enabled it can answer with a tool call instead. Settings in the code: model=Qwen3-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf.

hops.label: answer shown on screen
hops.explain: The response travels back the same way and the screen updates.

memoryMap.explain: CrossEncoder loads the model into RAM when it is created and keeps it there for the life of the process.
db keeps the search graph and the vectors it walks in RAM so a query touches a few hundred vectors in milliseconds.
embed loads the models it serves into RAM.
llm loads the models it serves into RAM.
lexical_search holds the word counts for every chunk in backend process's RAM; it is rebuilt when the process restarts.
bge-m3-Q8 loads the model into RAM when it is created and keeps it there for the life of the process.
db saves every collection to its data folder. No volume is mounted, so it is lost when the container is recreated.
